rationale: Both correctly explain the core attrgetter/dotted-path fix, but Y goes further: it independently reconstructs the exact regression history the GT reviewers discuss (pre-#5720 getattr chain vs post-#5720 breakage) and, crucially, extends the human parity argument (david6666666's 'mirrors module_collector.py' comment) into two concrete, code-level catches — the missing warning-on-failed-resolve that module_collector.py has but this PR's version lacks, and the missing id(module) dedup — closely tracking the GT reviewer's actual point rather than just gesturing at 'consistency'. Y also surfaces a substantive, specific correctness risk (SoulX Singer's mismatched-sequence-length CFG forwards now silently hitting DBCache) that X misses entirely. X's review is competent and well-organized but stays more generic/surface-level and its suggestions are vaguer (e.g., 'reword the warning', 'mirror the isinstance check') versus Y's precise line-level fixes.
